judgments.catchwords: CONSTRUCTION LAW — Adjudication — Stay pending setting-aside application — Filing of application opening discretion without conferring entitlement — Clear error and justice of relied upon to reject primary liquidated damages claim — Whether decisive plea introduced without fair opportunity to answer — Opportunity to argue for leave distinguished from substantive opportunity to respond — No automatic right to rejoinder — Complete procedural record requiring examination at setting-aside hearing — Construction Industry Payment and Adjudication Act 2012, s 15(b) CONSTRUCTION LAW — Adjudicator’s jurisdiction and impartiality — Retention entitlement and interest allegedly insufficiently pleaded — Unchanged quantum not excluding new contractual or jurisdictional basis — Refusal to revise certificates for insufficient material not itself refusal to adjudicate — Extension for reply and refusal of general rejoinder not themselves establishing partiality — Ultimate merits reserved — Construction Industry Payment and Adjudication Act 2012, ss 5(2), 15, 25 and 27 CONSTRUCTION LAW — Stay — Payee’s capacity to repay — Adjudicated sum substantially exceeding book shareholders’ funds and net current assets — Annual loss and incomplete current financial evidence — Neither probable non-recovery nor assured repayment established — Insolvency not mandatory gateway to stay — Recovery uncertainty relevant but insufficient alone — Construction Industry Payment and Adjudication Act 2012, s 16 EVIDENCE — Financial position — Company-search summary distinguished from current liquidity analysis — Positive net assets not proving commercial solvency — Absence of management accounts not automatically supporting adverse inference — Applicant retaining burden of proving repayment risk — Possible contribution of unpaid certified sums to financial difficulties unresolved — Evidence Act 1950, s 114 illustration (g) CONSTRUCTION LAW — Conditional stay — Deposit with Asian International Arbitration Centre — Security of RM9,135,151.96 comprising adjudicated sum and adjudication costs — Deposit required within fourteen days — Automatic lapse of stay upon non-compliance — Contractor’s loss of immediate cash flow weighed notwithstanding security — Expedited case management and liberty to seek variation — Construction Industry Payment and Adjudication Act 2012, s 16(2) CONSTRUCTION LAW — Adjudication interest — Stakeholder deposit not payment under award — Award interest continuing on specified principal amounts — Fixed security excluding further accrued and future interest — Fund earnings and releases to be credited without duplicate recovery — Release not discharging lawful shortfall CIVIL PROCEDURE — Scope and duration of stay — Restraint confined to recovery of identified adjudication award — No stay of unidentified existing judgment or execution order — Protection ending upon High Court’s disposal of setting-aside application — Stay through subsequent appeal refused — Further appellate stay requiring fresh application — Release of secured fund governed by outcome and further court orders

judgments.title: Shaharun Bin Ab Lattif v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: HABEAS CORPUS Application for writ of habeas corpus - Preventive detention - Validity of detention order - Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985 ('Act 316') - Whether detention unlawful - Whether writ ought to be issued. DANGEROUS DRUGS Preventive detention - Detention order under s 6(1) Act 316 - Involvement in distribution of dangerous drugs - "Large group of people" - Public order - Minister's satisfaction - Whether requirements of Art 149 Federal Constitution satisfied. JUDICIAL REVIEW Scope of review - Preventive detention - Section 11C(1) Act 316 - Whether court limited to procedural non-compliance - Subjective satisfaction of Minister - Whether merits of investigation reviewable. DANGEROUS DRUGS Statement recording - Section 4(5) Act 316 - Read-back requirement - Whether statement read back to detainee - Whether detainee given opportunity to make corrections - Mandatory procedural requirement - Whether complied with. EVIDENCE Forgery - Alleged forged signatures on recorded statement - Burden of proof - Absence of expert evidence - Absence of police report - Presumption of regularity - Whether forgery proven. ADMINISTRATIVE LAW Mala fide - Conflict of interest - Alleged intimidation by investigating officers - Whether allegations substantiated - Affidavit evidence - Public officers performing official duties. DANGEROUS DRUGS Advisory Board - Representation hearing - Regulation 10(2)(b) Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) (Advisory Board Procedure) Rules 1987 - Whether detainee denied right to be heard - Whether regulation ultra vires Act 316. DANGEROUS DRUGS Statutory reports - Delay in submission - Investigation report under s 3(3) - Inquiry Officer's report under s 5(4) - Whether delay constituted procedural non-compliance - Whether detention order invalidated. Held: Applicant failed to establish any material procedural non-compliance under Act 316; detention order valid; application for writ of habeas corpus dismissed.

judgments.catchwords: 1. The Plaintiff commenced this action against the Defendants. There is nothing unusual about a suit being filed. In the course of the proceedings, the 1st to 3rd Defendants succeeded in obtaining an order requiring the Plaintiff to furnish security for costs in the sum of RM80,000.00. That too, in itself, is nothing unusual. This was followed by the present application in Enclosure 34 by the Plaintiff for a stay of that order requiring the Plaintiff to furnish security for costs. Again, this is not an unusual application. The unusual feature of the present case lies in this. The order for security for costs was accompanied by an Unless Order, providing that the suit would be struck out if the security were not furnished within the prescribed period. More significantly, by the time the present application for a stay comes before this Court for hearing, that period has expired and the consequence stipulated by the Unless Order has already taken effect. 2. It is this sequence of events which gives rise to the difficulty in the present application. The Plaintiff filed Enclosure 34 before the time prescribed for furnishing the security had expired. However, no stay was obtained before that period expired and the Plaintiff did not furnish the security. The question which now arises is what relief, if any, remains available under Enclosure 34 when the application comes before this Court for determination after the consequence stipulated by the Unless Order has already taken effect. 3. This Court has considered the affidavits and written submissions filed by the Plaintiff and the 1st to 3rd Defendants, together with the authorities relied upon by both sides.
judgments.judge: YA Dr Choong Yeow Choy

judgments.catchwords: 1. The appeal is allowed in part. 2. As to the primary claim: The appeal against the award of RM10,888.00 and costs of RM2,000.00 is dismissed. The learned Magistrate's decision that the Appellant/Defendant shall pay the Respondent/Plaintiff the sum of RM10,888.00, with costs of RM2,000.00, is upheld. 3. As to the counterclaim: The appeal is allowed. The judgment of the learned Magistrate dismissing the Appellant's/Defendant's counterclaim is set aside. In its place, I enter an interlocutory judgment in favour of the Appellant/Defendant against the Respondent/Plaintiff, with liability of the Respondent/Plaintiff in negligence decided in the Appellant's/Defendant's favour. 4. Assessment of damages: Damages payable by the Respondent/Plaintiff to the Appellant/Defendant shall be remitted to the Magistrates' Court, Kuala Lumpur, for assessment of damages. Exemplary and punitive damages are excluded. 5. Costs: As both parties have succeeded in part the Appellant on the counterclaim and the Respondent on the contract limb I make no order as to the costs of this appeal. Each party shall bear its own costs. Costs in the Magistrates' Court shall remain as ordered.

judgments.title: CHONG YOON SZE & ors v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Prosedur Jenayah — Rayuan terhadap sabitan dan hukuman — Perayu-perayu didakwa dengan pertuduhan mengedar dadah berbahaya di bawah seksyen 39B(1)(a) Akta Dadah Berbahaya 1952 (ADB). Keterangan – sama ada HMT terkhilaf apabila memutuskan bahawa milikan dan jagaan berjaya dibuktikan oleh pihak pendakwaan. Sama ada elemen pengetahuan berjaya dibuktikan oleh pihak pendakwaan. Sama ada perayu-perayu mempunyai niat bersama dan membuat apa-apa "overt act" bagi tujuan pengedaran. Sama ada terdapat kebergantungan yang tidak wajar terhadap tingkah laku atau maklumat yang membawa kepada penemuan dadah, penerimaan bukti yang tidak boleh diterima.

judgments.title: BELLWORTH DEVELOPMENTS SDN BHD v SETIAKON BUILDERS SDN BHD
judgments.catchwords: The Court of Appeal reaffirmed the principle of minimal judicial intervention in arbitration. A procedural breach, such as an alleged one-day delay in submitting a draft award for AIAC technical review, does not automatically invalidate an arbitral award where the requirement is merely directory, no timely objection was raised, and no prejudice is shown. An arbitral award will not be set aside on the basis of a purported “new difference” where the issue was within the parties’ pleadings, evidence and submissions. Courts will not review the merits of an award under the guise of a setting-aside application.’

judgments.title: Pendakwa Raya & ors v AZRIL SANI BIN RAMUDIN & ors
judgments.catchwords: Pertuduhan asal di Mahkamah Tinggi ialah dua pertuduhan di bawah seksyen 39B(1)(a) Akta Dadah Berbahaya (ADB) - OKT Azril Sani dan OKT Aizad Imran telah dituduh bersama-sama - Di akhir kes Pembelaan, HMT telah melepaskan dan membebaskan OKT Aizad Imran daripada kedua-dua pertuduhan, manakala terhadap OKT Azril Sani, HMT telah meminda pertuduhan kepada seksyen 6 ADB dan seksyen 12(2) ADB masing-masing dihukum di bawah seksyen 39A(2) ADB - Di Mahkamah Rayuan, OKT Azril Sani merayu terhadap sabitan dan hukuman, manakala pihak Pendakwaan merayu terhadap keputusan HMT meminda pertuduhan asal terhadap OKT Azril Sani dan keputusan HMT yang melepaskan dan membebaskan OKT Aizad Imran - Isu sama ada HMT terkhilaf dalam membuat dapatan tiada perbuatan terangan atau “overt act” oleh kedua-dua Tertuduh dalam mengedar dadah itu sedangkan HMT telah menggunapakai anggapan perbuatan mengedar dadah di bawah seksyen 37(da)(vi) dan (xvi) ADB.
